requirements.requirement: Provide an HTTP forward proxy on node1 TCP port 3128 that node2 can use to retrieve the approved handbook from the legacy origin.
requirements.summary: Squid was installed and configured on node1, was active and listening on port 3128, and node2 retrieved the approved handbook through it with HTTP 200. The same behavior succeeded after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Permit proxy requests only to the node2 origin on TCP 8081, rejecting other destination ports and all CONNECT tunnels.
requirements.summary: The configured policy allows only node2 as client and node2:8081 as destination, denies CONNECT before the allow rule, and denies everything else. Direct tests returned 403 for an alternate destination port and for CONNECT before and after restarts; Squid's access log confirms the allowed and denied outcomes.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the staged legacy origin application and make its approved handbook reachable through the proxy from node2.
requirements.summary: The handbook and server-script hashes match the preparation baseline. The origin service was active on port 8081, returned the expected handbook, and recovered with unchanged files and data after node2 restarted; retrieval through the proxy also recovered.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 after implementation and restart. Squid 5.5 was installed from the AlmaLinux AppStream repository, and the supplied origin ran under the installed Python 3.9.21.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence, including recovery after sequential node restarts. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart scheduling acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, policy behavior, files, and data.
limitations: Only one representative disallowed destination port, TCP 8080, was behaviorally tested. The deny-all Squid rule directly supports rejection of all remaining unapproved ports, but they were not exhaustively probed.

The lifecycle snapshots inventory sockets and system health but do not independently capture persistent firewall configuration; firewall rules were instead directly observed by executor commands after restart.
A small validation artifact, /tmp/squid-parse.out, remained on node1.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear task or mandatory evidence roles: installing Squid, configuring and enabling the proxy and origin services, adding source-restricted firewall rules, and performing the required restarts. No unnecessary troubleshooting mutations were identified. Services recovered without failed units, package checks remained healthy, and network access was restricted by application policy and source-specific firewall rules. The only minor residue is /tmp/squid-parse.out, created by the post-restart configuration-validation command and not cleaned; it remained after execution but was a bounded, low-risk evidence artifact rather than an unrelated mutation.
